title: Optimal Bounds for Open Addressing Without Reordering
authors: Martín Farach-Colton (New York University, USA), Andrew Krapivin (Cambridge University, UK), William Kuszmaul (Carnegie Mellon University, USA)
abstract: In this paper, we revisit one of the simplest problems in data structures: the task of inserting elements into an open-addressed hash table so that elements can later be retrieved with as few probes as possible. We show that, even without reordering elements over time, it is possible to construct a hash table that achieves far better expected search complexities (both amortized and worst-case) than were previously thought possible. Along the way, we disprove the central conjecture left by Yao in his seminal paper \emph{``Uniform Hashing is Optimal''}.
